summary: Shōkō Kabutogi worked in Buddhist studies. He studied at Rissho University from circa 1933 to 1936 and served as a professor there from circa 1950 to 1982.
Shūei Tsuboi was a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a professor at Bukkyo University, attested in 1963 and 1972.

Shūichi Katō studied at the University of Tokyo (~1940–1943) and worked in Japanology and philosophy. He held posts at the University of Tokyo, UBC (~1960–1969), Free University of Berlin (~1969–1973), Sophia (~1974–1979), Yale (~1979–1984), and Ritsumeikan (~1993–2008).

Si Ti La is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a PhD at Acharya Nagarjuna University under J. Sitaramamma. He also studied under ten traditional teachers, including U Kundala, U Sajjanasāra, and U Sāsana.
Sibani Dasgupta studied Indology at the University of Dhaka and completed a doctorate at the University of Calcutta by 1954 under Sushil Kumar De. She also studied under Rajendra Chandra Hazra.

Sibraj Chetry works in philosophy and Buddhist studies, having studied under doctoral supervisor Sibnath Sarma and teachers D. K. Chakravarty, N. Sharma, Girish Sarma, and M. Boruah. He was a lecturer of philosophy at North Lakhimpur College in 2012.

Siegfried Goldschmidt worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Albrecht Weber in 1864, Rudolf von Roth from circa 1864 to 1867, and at the University of Tübingen in 1867. He also taught Heinrich Zimmer.

Siegfried Lienhard was an Indologist who studied at the University of Vienna (~1943–1949). He held posts at the University of Kiel (~1962–1967) and Stockholm University (attested 1991), and he taught Leif Asplund.

Siglinde Dietz works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology, having earned her PhD at the University of Bonn under Michael Hahn by 1980. She held a post at the University of Göttingen (attested 1990) and taught Ryutaro Tsuchida and Andrey Klebanov.
Signe Howell studied at the University of Oxford (~1976–1980) and worked in religious studies. She held a post at the University of Oslo from circa 1987 to 2012 and taught Heidi Fjeld.
Sik Fanin works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She earned a PhD from Lancaster University by 2008 and served as a teaching consultant at the University of Hong Kong, attested in 2013.

Silvio Vita studied at University of Naples "L'Orientale" (1973–1978) and Princeton (1983–1986). Working in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology, he held posts at "L'Orientale", Naples Federico II, Sapienza, Kyoto University of Foreign Studies, and directed ISEAS (~2000–2018).
Simo Parpola is a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology. He served as Professor of Assyriology at the University of Helsinki from circa 1979 to 2009.

Simon P. James works in philosophy and religious studies. He taught Colette Sciberras and held posts at Durham University as a tutor in philosophy (attested 2001) and lecturer in philosophy (attested 2013–2014).
Singhathon Narāsabho is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned a PhD at Visva-Bharati University under the supervision of Sudhindra Chandra Chakravarti (attested 1971).

Siniruddha Dash works in Indology and linguistics. He served as Head of the Department of Sanskrit at the University of Madras (2000–2014; attested 2022) and was Director of the Oriental Research Institute, Mysore, attested in 2013.

Sisir Roy works in philosophy, having studied under Debabrata SenSharma. He held posts at the Indian Statistical Institute as a professor and at the National Institute of Advanced Studies, both attested in 2009.
Siu-tong Kwan is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned a PhD from the University of Hong Kong under doctoral supervisor K. L. Dhammajoti and also studied under Zhihua Yao in 2005.

So Takahashi studied at the University of Tokyo, receiving an M.A., and specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Meijo University as an associate professor (attested 1977–1978) and as a professor (attested 1991).

Sodo Mori studied at the University of Tokyo (~1957–1968). A scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, he was a professor at Aichi Gakuin University (~1986–2005), lecturer at Toyo and Taisho universities (1985), and Pali Text Society Japan representative (1985).
